searchText: feel free to redirect me since this might not be the right channel, but in support of 4844 I want to get some continuous profiling going for both geth and prysm -- I'll add some of this instrumentation in my own fork but is there any general guidance for adding dependencies and tools that most likely will not be used in production (i.e. on mainnet nodes)? I was looking at Pyroscope which has a really nice and intuitive UI (https://pyroscope.io/docs/golang/) which I'll expose on my own servers and make available as a dev resource specifically, there's some config that needs to go in code that will be off by default but it's still extra code 🤷‍♂️ prysm supports profling with `--pprof` flag, then you can use the UI like `go tool pprof -http localhost:7078 http://localhost:6060/debug/pprof/profile` not as pretty as Pyroscope though

excerpts.content:
feel free to redirect me since this might not be the right channel, but in support of 4844 I want to get some continuous profiling going for both geth and prysm -- I'll add some of this instrumentation in my own fork but is there any general guidance for adding dependencies and tools that most likely will not be used in production (i.e. on mainnet nodes)?
I was looking at Pyroscope which has a really nice and intuitive UI (https://pyroscope.io/docs/golang/) which I'll expose on my own servers and make available as a dev resource

specifically, there's some config that needs to go in code that will be off by default but it's still extra code 🤷‍♂️

excerpts.content: prysm supports profling with `--pprof` flag, then you can use the UI like `go tool pprof -http localhost:7078  http://localhost:6060/debug/pprof/profile`
